output.brief:
The October night premium shortfalls were caused by a pay-rule change, not by your data. On 22 Oct an Ardentra consultant applied a standard template to the night premium rule (NSP-02). It was logged as a label correction, but it also moved the premium start time from 20:00 to 22:00. The platform audit trail shows this was the only calculation change. Internal audit's recalculation found 147 of 158 night workers underpaid, each by exactly the 20:00–22:00 hours. The 11 correctly paid staff work 22:00–06:00. Ardentra's own test system pays correctly once the start time is set back to 20:00. Flagged records show no higher underpayment rate than unflagged ones, so the data explanation fails. Release 7.4 and the bank file are not implicated.

What to do: don't suspend the HR team, don't run a full re-cleanse, and don't accept the clause 14.3 cost. Have Ardentra restore the 20:00 start and verify it in the test system before 24 Nov. Then pay all underpaid staff, including the 8 who didn't complain, through an off-cycle payment. Hold Ardentra to account for the unflagged change. Don't roll back 7.4. The overtime drop may be partly caused by the pay issue and partly by the rota trial. Fix the pay first, then see whether cover recovers before deciding on the trial.
